newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy advertisers see billings rising 9pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Italy advertisers see billings rising 9pct in 1996.

text.p: Italian advertisers expect billings to rise nine percent in 1996, confirming the industry is emerging from years of crisis, the national trade body said on Thursday.

Alberto Contri, chairman of the Italian Association of Advertising and Communications Consultancies (AssAP), told an industry conference the market now faced a transition period in adapting to the impact of new technologies, like the internet.
He described advertising in Italy as "20 years of glory, some five years of deep crisis from which we seem to be emerging this year -- with a nine percent growth of total advertising expenditure."

Two-thirds of Italian advertising executives shared the upbeat assessment of industry ratings groups, which have forecast an eight percent rise in the market this year, according to a survey carried out by AssAP.

In the survey, which polled 100 advertisers from Italy's top agencies, 46 percent of respondents said the internet and other multimedia technology had already begun to have an impact on their agencies' creativity.
But 32 percent said they expected the new interactive media to have only "minimal" impact on their activities.
The figures were released at the annual meeting of the European Association of Advertising Agencies, which groups advertising and trade bodies from 24 countries.
